_generated: Written by `autowork setup`. Shared gates come from autowork/profile_template.json; everything else is yours.

constraints._age_note: The whole premise is applying into short queues. A posting older than ~6 weeks has either been filled or has a queue hundreds deep, so it is gated out rather than merely scored down.
constraints._role_note: Not engineering, or not the right kind. 'Associate TSE II' and 'Technical Support Engineer (Inference)' both scored highly on keyword overlap before this existed — the JD talks about Kubernetes because you would be supporting it, not building it.
constraints._levels_note: Matched only as a trailing level token so 'Engineer 3' and 'SDE-2' are blocked while 'Vue 3', 'Go 1.22' and 'Web3' are not.
constraints._exemption_note: Phrases neutralised before the seniority scan. 'Member of Technical Staff' is not a level — it is what OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Sierra and Cockroach Labs call engineers at every band — but it trips the 'staff' block term, which silently rejected 126 postings. Stripping the phrase leaves the real modifiers intact, so 'Senior Member of Technical Staff' is still blocked on 'senior'.
constraints._location_note: A posting qualifies if it names an India location, or is remote without being scoped to a foreign region. 'Remote - USA' is rejected; bare 'Remote' is kept.
constraints._block_levels_note: Applied to level_hint, which is the source's own grading (LinkedIn's job_level, SmartRecruiters' experienceLevel). More reliable than inferring a band from the title, so it is checked first and short-circuits the regex.
constraints._family_note: Which kind of job counts. Selects a role_families entry: its title_pattern is the allowlist and its block_role_terms the refinement. 'any' disables the allowlist for fields not listed.

signals._comment: Cross-cutting adjustments applied after the per-profile skill score.
signals._signals_note: Both families present is the sweet spot — infra depth valued inside a product team. A pure-ops title with no product language is penalised, since it is explicitly not what is wanted.
signals._ai_note: Agent/LLM product experience is the rarest thing on the resume; postings that need it are where the candidate is most differentiated.

job_search._comment: Keyword search via JobSpy. Measured: of its eight boards only LinkedIn and Indeed return anything for India. Naukri gives 406 recaptcha; Glassdoor, Google, ZipRecruiter and Bayt return zero rows. Indeed is off by default — it has volume but is noisier and rate-limits after ~8 queries from one IP.
job_search._cost_note: LinkedIn fetches each description as a separate request, so the poll goes from ~20s to several minutes. Descriptions are not optional — the experience bar lives in them — so the lever is results_per_term. 4 terms x 25 keeps the run inside the workflow timeout with margin.
